At its peak, this company had more than nine thousand stores. Then it laughed at Netflix. This is how Blockbuster ruled Friday night. Dallas, Texas, nineteen eighty five. A man named David Cook opened a new kind of video store. His was huge, bright, and full of thousands of tapes. A businessman named Wayne Huizenga bought in. At one point, a new Blockbuster opened somewhere about every seventeen hours. Blockbuster became a ritual. Walking the aisles. Grabbing popcorn and candy at the counter. Every tape had a sticker that said, be kind, rewind. And if you brought it back late, you paid. Late fees made Blockbuster hundreds of millions of dollars a year. Those late fees made a lot of people angry. One of them was Reed Hastings. In nineteen ninety seven, he started Netflix. DVDs arrived in the mail, in a little red envelope.
